articles.title: Farhan Akhtar, Ashutosh Gowariker and Madhur Bhandarkar Look Back at ‘Dil Chahta Hai,’ ‘Lagaan’ and ‘Chandni Bar’ at 25
articles.summary: In 2001, three films challenged familiar conventions of Hindi-language cinema in very different ways. Farhan Akhtar’s “Dil Chahta Hai” offered a new screen language for friendship and young adulthood; Ashutosh Gowariker’s “Lagaan” turned a village cricket match into an epic about resistance; and…
body: One thread connected their stories: all three had encountered the expectations of commercial Hindi cinema before finding the conviction to make something different.

Gowariker and Bhandarkar already had films behind them before “Lagaan” and “Chandni Bar” established their identities as filmmakers. Akhtar, making his directorial debut with “Dil Chahta Hai,” said he had not been interested in making a film that conformed to the prevailing Bollywood potboiler template.

For Gowariker, who is also the IFFI festival director this year, the turning point came after his first two films failed. Having initially tried to make commercial entertainers, he realized that “my next film had to be something I believe in, something that I want to make first, and then hope to God that the audience also likes it. So that’s how the genesis of ‘Lagaan’ happened.”

articles.title: NBC Pulls Spot Advocating for End of U.S. Military Aid to Israel, Will Review Approval Procedures After Outcry
articles.summary: NBC has pulled an ad from a Middle East advocacy organization that calls for the end of U.S. military aid to Israel. The network will review its ad approval procedures after criticism from the Simon Wiesenthal Center and other organizations.
body: The ad makes a jarring juxtaposition between the suffering in Gaza and scenes of a typical American preteen girl doing chores and odd jobs to save money for a bicycle amid tough economic times. Just as the American girl brings her jar full of money into a bike shop, the spot cuts to a scene of a girl standing in a pile of rubble in Gaza. As the camera pans back, the girl is revealed to be leaning on a crutch, having lost one of her lower legs. The spot tells viewers that “Every three seconds” the U.S. sends about $400 million in military aid to Israel under a long-term deal set to expire in 2028.
NBC’s top brass were unaware of the spot before it aired. As a result, there will be a review of the network’s ad approval processes, according to a person familiar with the situation.

Jim Berk, CEO of the Wiesenthal Center, issued a lengthy statement on Thursday questioning NBC’s decision to air the ad during an “SNL” entertainment special in primetime. He pointed to the ad’s potential to fuel hostility against Israel and Jews.
points: NBC has pulled an ad from a Middle East advocacy organization that calls for the end of U.S. military aid to Israel.
The network will review its ad approval procedures after criticism from the Simon Wiesenthal Center and other organizations.

articles.title: Predicting Awards Season’s First Big Week: Who Wins at the Gothams, NYFCC, NBR and More
articles.summary: The starting gun of the Oscar season starts Monday, and by next Sunday, it will have a shape that many of us will be able to see clearly. For months, the Oscar race has run on festival premieres, studio screenings and ever more elaborate predictions, mine included.
body: The Gothams, the New York Film Critics Circle, the National Board of Review, the American Film Institute and LAFCA each answer to a different electorate and each has its own complicated history with the Academy. None of them pick the Oscars, but they all shape the conversation that follows.
The question isn’t only who wins. It’s who wins where, and what each victory says about the corner of the electorate that handed it out.
Here’s how we see the opening week unfolding, with some commentary for each.

The Gothams have long been a launching pad for independent cinema, a place for films that might otherwise get flattened by the studio machine. In 2023, the organization scrapped its $35 million budget ceiling and opened more categories to international titles. The result is a more eclectic ballot, one that puts established auteurs and first-time filmmakers side by side. This year, that means 42 features and 25 performances across 11 categories.

articles.title: ‘Percy Jackson and the Olympians’ Star Leah Sava Jeffries on Her Idea for Annabeth’s Gray Contacts and the Big Fan Surprise Coming in the Season 3 Finale: A ‘Dream Came True’
articles.summary: SPOILER ALERT: The following story contains plot details from “I Learn How to Grow Zombies,” Season 3, Episode 3 of “Percy Jackson and the Olympians,” now streaming on Disney+.
body: The Season 3 premiere saw Jeffries’ Annabeth kidnapped by a human-lion-scorpion hybrid monster called a manticore and taken across the country from Percy ( Walker Scobell ) and Grover (Aryan Simhadri). Annabeth faces her own struggles while her friends work to rescue her, which is new for the show; the first two seasons followed the trio going on epic quests together. With Annabeth separated for much of “The Titan’s Curse” — the third book in Rick Riordan’s “Percy Jackson” series, which Season 3 is based on — Jeffries’ main scene partners now are Charlie Bushnell, who plays Luke, and Dafne Keen, who plays Artemis.

That’s not the only way Season 3 is wading into uncharted waters. The first-ever screen interpretation of “Percy Jackson” was a pair of movies in the early 2010s based on Riordan’s first and second books. But Jeffries is keenly aware of the fact that “The Titan’s Curse” has never been adapted.

articles.title: The little Welsh town that transformed a Strictly star's career
articles.summary: Layton Williams credits living and working in a small Welsh town with transforming his career.
body: The Bad Education actor spent months in Mold, Flintshire, rehearsing for the role of Angel in the musical Rent, which he said marked a turning point in his career.
"I've got to be honest, before I lived in Mold, I had not a clue that Mold was a place that existed, but I completely fell in love with it," he said.
Williams, from Bury in Greater Manchester, feels so connected to the town that he insisted on having a show at the Theatr Clwyd on his upcoming tour, Layton Live.
"The producers were like, 'we've never had a specific request to go to Mold, but we will make it happen'. And I said 'Thank you'," Williams said in an interview with Lucy Owen on BBC Radio Wales.

articles.title: Avengers: Doomsday has brought with it more ‘Marvel homework’ than ever. That’s just as it should be
articles.summary: Working out where returning hero Steve Rogers has been is only one of the multiversal puzzles fans must now get their heads around – which is catnip for the connoisseurs.
body: The cinema release of Avengers: Doomsday is now roughly three weeks away and, judging by the final trailer, we’re living in the one timeline where every loose end Marvel has left dangling for years is now worth tugging on. Even the ones we thought the studio had tied up rather nicely. Ever since it became apparent that Chris Evans’ Steve Rogers would be returning in the new film, along with next year’s sequel Avengers: Secret Wars, fans have been asking themselves: where exactly has he been all this time? Now, thanks to the latest footage, we’re beginning to get an idea, and we might also be starting to pick up clues as to why Doctor Doom would take an interest in his new postcode.

One of the most startling aspects of the new trailer is the arrival of the Fantastic Four, led by Pedro Pascal’s Reed Richards, on Rogers’ front lawn. We’ve known since the finale of Avengers: Endgame that Steve used Tony Stark’s newly discovered time-travelling tech to go back to the 1940s and live out his life with Peggy Carter during the events of that film – but until recently it seemed most likely that happened in good old Earth-616, the main Marvel Cinematic Universe continuity.

articles.title: Alun Wyn Jones urges men to talk about hair loss after transplant
articles.summary: The former Wales captain said he wanted to encourage more men to talk openly about hair loss.
body: Rugby legend Alun Wyn Jones has urged men to open up about hair loss, saying he was "very comfortable" talking about the fact he has had a hair transplant.
Speaking one year since his operation, the former Wales and British and Irish Lions captain said men typically do not talk about the issue, but said "a lot of people" had spoken to him about it.
"I think it's important that people know there's a lot of people out there they can talk to," he said.
Jones played 158 times for Wales and 12 for the Lions, making him the most capped rugby player in history before he retired in 2023.

articles.title: Cozy escapism or festive trash? How Netflix holiday movies took over Christmas
articles.summary: The so-bad-it’s-good holiday film has become a new festive tradition. Stars Maddie Ziegler and Dennis Quaid explain why they’re so hard to resist. “With the state of the world right now, people want an escape,” says Maddie Ziegler.
body: In the film, Ziegler plays Maelyn – a restless twentysomething who finds herself trapped in a holiday time-loop, where she’s forced to relive the same Christmas at her family’s picturesque cabin until she learns to trust her gut and take chances on what makes her happy. This sugary-sweet movie might be new territory for Ziegler, but it’s exactly the type of film we’ve come to expect from Netflix. The streamer’s Christmas originals usually revolve around romance and family, with an aesthetic quality and winking irony that feels similar to Hallmark – the American card-maker turned movie giant, whose very name is synonymous with cliches.

In fact, Padalecki thinks Netflix might have tapped him for this project because the millennial ritual of rewatching the show makes him feel innately familiar to people. “With TV, you’re in their home, you’re playing in the background when they’re cooking dinner, or they’re taking out the garbage, or helping their kids with homework,” he says. “And as they’re doing that, they’re hearing your voice.”

articles.title: Rare panto programmes owned by 'Freddie Mercury of his time' sell at auction
articles.summary: The life of Henry Paget was the focus of the biopic Madfabulous released earlier this year.
body: A rare pair of pantomime programmes from the private theatre of a man dubbed "the Freddie Mercury of his time" have sold at auction for £3,600.
The 4th Marquess of Anglesey Henry Cyril Paget, also known as the Dancing Marquess, used his family home Plas Newydd, on Anglesey, to stage lavish productions free for local people.
His life was recently turned into a biopic, with Callum Scott Howells playing the aristocrat.
The programmes were for a production of Red Riding Hood and in the shapes of Little Red Riding Hood and Little Boy Blue.

articles.title: Get me a 747 and deploy the oxygen masks! The British pilot behind Hollywood’s greatest inflight scenes
articles.summary: An emergency landing for Bridesmaids, a humiliation for Ben Stiller in Focker-in-Law, a giant toilet for Britney Spears in the Toxic video … Richard Chan, No 1 provider of airplane cabin sets, recalls his finest work.
body: With Thanksgiving having just kicked off holiday season in the US, millions of people are boarding flights, many more concerned than ever about how chaotic that might be. Aside from the shock of the recent FAA shutdown, not a day seems to go by without a viral video of someone behaving badly or being removed from an airplane: Saturday Night Live even did a sketch about the introduction of a “new airline class”, with a whole section of a plane reserved for “crazy people”.

In the big Thanksgiving movie Focker-In-Law, Ben Stiller has a lengthy and awkward encounter with a flight attendant who is summoned by a passenger called Olivia, played by Ariana Grande. On arrival, he learns that Olivia is his potential daughter-in-law and, of course, that means more trouble with his ex-CIA father-in-law Jack, played by Robert De Niro.
